questions.stem: When measuring mass loss during a gas-producing reaction, why is cotton wool placed in the top of the flask?

options.text: To prevent splashing of liquid while still allowing gas to escape
To keep the temperature constant inside the flask
To absorb the gas produced and prevent it escaping
To act as a catalyst for the reaction

questions.explanation: Cotton wool is placed loosely in the top of the flask to prevent liquid from splashing out while still allowing the gas to escape. This ensures the mass decrease measured on the balance is only due to gas escaping, not liquid being lost.
